# mcrl log

[Command reference](README.md)

Search logs.

```text
Aliases:
  log, logs
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| [`log saved`](#mcrl-log-saved) | List saved log searches |
| [`log search`](#mcrl-log-search) | Search logs |

## mcrl log saved

List saved log searches.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl log saved

List saved log searches.

API: GET /api/v0/saved-log-searches
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl log saved
  mcrl log saved --jq '.[] | {name, definition}'
```

## mcrl log search

Search logs.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl log search --service <service> [flags]

Search logs of a service, newest first.

The range is --since (default 15 minutes ago) to --until (exclusive), at most
30 days. --keyword matches text in the body; --where matches fields of JSON
bodies, with the type inferred from the value. With -o jsonl the results are
printed as each page arrives. The API allows 1 request per second, so large
--limit values take a while.

API: POST /api/v0/logs, GET /api/v0/saved-log-searches (--saved)
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl log search --service web --severity error+
  mcrl log search --service web --since 1h --where 'res.status>=500' --where 'req.method=POST'
  mcrl log search --saved 'checkout errors' --since 7d --limit 0 -o jsonl > errors.jsonl

Flags:
      --asc                    oldest first (default: newest first)
      --keyword stringArray    text the body contains (repeatable; all must match)
      --limit int              maximum number of log entries (0 = all) (default 100)
      --namespace string       service namespace (service.namespace)
      --saved string           start from a saved log search (ID or name); flags override its conditions
      --service string         service name (the service.name resource attribute)
      --severity stringArray   severity, comma-separated or repeated; "warn+" means WARN and above
      --since string           start of the time range (at most 30 days before --until) (default "15m")
      --trace-id string        trace ID (32 hex characters)
      --until string           end of the time range (exclusive) (default "now")
      --where stringArray      condition on a JSON body field, e.g. "res.status>=500", "req.method=GET", "path^=/api" (repeatable)
```

## mcrl log tail

Follow new logs.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl log tail --service <service> [flags]

Print recent logs, then keep printing new ones as they arrive, oldest first,
one JSON object per line. Stop with Ctrl-C.

The API is polled every --interval (at least 1 second; the API allows 1
request per second). Logs that arrive late, with a timestamp older than ones
already printed, may be missed.

API: POST /api/v0/logs
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl log tail --service web
  mcrl log tail --service web --severity warn+ --jq '[.timestamp, .severity, .body] | @tsv'

Flags:
      --interval duration      polling interval (1s or more) (default 2s)
      --keyword stringArray    text the body contains (repeatable; all must match)
      --namespace string       service namespace (service.namespace)
      --saved string           start from a saved log search (ID or name); flags override its conditions
      --service string         service name (the service.name resource attribute)
      --severity stringArray   severity, comma-separated or repeated; "warn+" means WARN and above
      --since string           show logs from this time before following (default "1m")
      --trace-id string        trace ID (32 hex characters)
      --where stringArray      condition on a JSON body field, e.g. "res.status>=500", "req.method=GET", "path^=/api" (repeatable)
```
